clue.text: Minutes consumed by change to the rear part of engine

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed up, so the first item ends up inside what follows

parts.note: loose change is coins, that is, cash
M is the standard abbreviation for minutes
aft is the nautical word for towards the back

explanation.surface: A mechanic grumbles that minutes are lost to changing the back of an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' reads as a verb about repairs, but it is the noun for coins. Aft is the sailor's word for the back of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is the rotating rod in a motor whose lobes open and close the valves.

clue.text: Bully declines flowers

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them
standards that decline are said to slip

explanation.surface: A thug's power fades over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowslips are yellow spring wildflowers of the primrose family, so they are examples of flowers.

clue.text: Some caviare simply upset skinflint

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the run of letters reads backwards
only some of the letters of the following words are used, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words, from the end of the first into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A tightwad is annoyed at how plain the caviar is.
explanation.walkthrough: caviaRE SIMply holds RESIM; read upwards it gives MISER.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a stingy person who hoards money, exactly what a miser is.

clue.text: Temper hot before strike, not cold

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: not cold tells us to leave out the letter abbreviating cold from the word for strike

parts.note: to cuff is to hit with an open hand
C stands for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry before lashing out, the opposite of keeping cool.
explanation.walkthrough: H and C for hot and cold come from the labels on taps.
explanation.definitionFit: A huff is a fit of petty annoyance or sulking, a bad temper.

clue.text: Cutting down, accepting small payment, getting sympathy

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: felling is cutting down trees
a payment that is small is a low fee

explanation.surface: A lumberjack paid a pittance for cutting trees wins people's sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: The small payment is two words, a low fee, and it lands in the middle of the tree-cutting word rather than at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow feeling is sympathy arising from shared experience with another person.

clue.text: Father with problems making additions

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
ills are troubles or misfortunes

explanation.surface: Dad's troubles keep piling up.
explanation.definitionFit: Frills are unnecessary extras or embellishments added to something basic.

clue.text: Bonds with tutor during periods of relaxation

indicators.note: during places one thing within the span of another, so it sits inside

parts.note: rests are breaks for relaxing
to tutor someone is to train or coach them

explanation.surface: Students bond with their teacher during breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraints are ties or shackles that hold someone, which bonds also are.

clue.text: Heartless person, one disrupting settled area in country

indicators.note: something disrupting a thing breaks into it, ending up inside

parts.note: a bird that lit on a branch settled there
A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: without its heart, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: a person is a human
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unfeeling individual causes trouble in a settled district of some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Settled is the past tense of alight, as a bird does on a perch, not the adjective for an established community.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a Baltic republic in north-eastern Europe, one of the three Baltic states.

clue.text: Fool imprisoned by state for reason

indicators.note: a prisoner is locked inside, so the first item goes within the second

parts.note: to state something is to say it
a nit is a silly person, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: An idiot has been locked up by the government on some grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a nation in the surface, but it works as the verb meaning declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of a sound mind, as in losing one's reason, is sanity.

clue.text: Melancholy? Fantastic news lifts us

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Feeling down? Some wonderful news cheers us up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the definition; the rest reads as a cheerful reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistfulness is a vague, regretful longing, a gentle kind of sadness or melancholy.

clue.text: Place in Cheshire magazine's story occupied by me

indicators.note: a building occupied by someone has them inside it, so the last item goes within

parts.note: Elle is a fashion magazine, and a report is a news story
taken as written

explanation.surface: A journalist boasts that a magazine article about a Cheshire town was written by them.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine's story is read as one two-word phrase, and the insertion splits it at the apostrophe. Cheshire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellesmere Port is an industrial town on the Manchester Ship Canal in Cheshire, England.

clue.text: Number in catch returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so read the word backwards

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: A cricket score counts the catches thrown back.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: any whole figure used for counting qualifies, and this is one such figure.

clue.text: Note by doctor about fat

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in an about-face, so this word runs backwards

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's memo concerns a patient's weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the doctor turns round; the note stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking, a type of fat.

clue.text: One in trouble is ordered to get garment for work

indicators.note: the word in simply places one item inside the following phrase
ordered means put in a new arrangement, so the letters are re-sorted

parts.note: the letters taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone in difficulty is told to put on overalls.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside the letters of TROUBLE IS, and all ten are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler suit is a one-piece overall worn over clothes for manual or dirty work.

clue.text: Seize facts I once distorted

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to having twisted the truth in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To confiscate is to take property by authority, which is to seize it.

clue.text: Standard form filled with nonsense automatically

indicators.note: something filled with stuff holds it inside, so that word sits within

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf
a form or manner of doing something is a fashion
rot is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: An official template is stuffed with gibberish without anyone thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Standard and form look like one phrase, a standard form, but they are two separate pieces with the nonsense pushed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning parrot-fashion means repeating by rote without understanding, done mechanically or automatically.

clue.text: Upset about inspector and copper being mocked

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: riled means annoyed or upset
DI is a Detective Inspector in British police
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Annoyed over a detective and a police officer making fun of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like another policeman; it is the metal, by its chemical symbol. 'Upset' is not an anagram signal here but the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridiculed means mocked or derided; the definition is the passive participle phrase.

clue.text: Poet in New York amid anxiety missing one

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the first item sits inside
missing one says the word is lacking the letter for one

parts.note: tension is nervous strain
the Roman numeral for one
the standard abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A writer of verse in Manhattan, nervous about someone absent.
explanation.walkthrough: The anxiety word loses a letter, then takes the city abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate, author of In Memoriam.

clue.text: Distinguish fat-free diet in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast originally meant scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn about

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Telling apart the low-fat regimen featured in a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but its two letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To differentiate is to recognise the difference between things, which is what distinguishing means.

clue.text: Old online journal assuming new shape

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the word takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a blog is a web log, an online diary
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A dated internet diary gets a fresh look.
explanation.walkthrough: O, then BLOG with N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle with unequal sides, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Poor clerk is bad one returning to sinful ways

indicators.note: poor means badly done, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A shabby office worker has gone bad again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like it could be the anagram signal; it is fodder, and 'Poor' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A backslider is someone who relapses into bad habits or sin after reforming.

clue.text: Revolution bites back

indicators.note: back here means backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: a nip is a small bite

explanation.surface: An uprising snaps back at its rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is one turn round an axis, a single revolution.

clue.text: Put down cheap wine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to set something down heavily
second meaning: British slang for inexpensive wine

explanation.surface: Someone puts down a bottle of plonk, or sneers at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests disparaging, but here it means dumping something down with a thud.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk is to set something down heavily; as a noun it is informal British for cheap wine.

clue.text: Part of Indonesia vital to global industry

indicators.note: vital also means at the core, so the letters lie at the heart of the following words

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A region of Indonesia matters greatly to world business.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is a province and island of Indonesia, famous for tourism.

clue.text: Bird in line following duck west

indicators.note: following places the first piece named after the ones named next

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, zero
W is the compass abbreviation for west
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A bird queues up behind a duck heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird; it is cricket's zero, as O.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is a nocturnal bird of prey with large forward-facing eyes.

clue.text: An explanation about a vote concerning Germanic people

indicators.note: about means around, so the word wraps the pieces that follow

parts.note: taken as written
a gloss is an explanatory note on a text
taken as written
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper
on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: An account of an election concerning a tribe from northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: AN, then GLOSS wrapping A, X and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxons were the Germanic tribes who settled in England from the fifth century.

clue.text: Device wrongly tagged

indicators.note: wrongly means incorrectly arranged, so the letters need re-sorting

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An item of equipment has the wrong label on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small mechanical or electronic contrivance, a handy device.

clue.text: Wounded from time with resistance in revolt

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the following word

parts.note: to revolt someone is to disgust or sicken them
T is the abbreviation for time
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Injured fighters stood their ground in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolt' looks like a reversal signal or an uprising; it is the verb meaning disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken describes someone struck down, hurt or afflicted, close to wounded.
